question: The North-South National Highway Corridor connects which two UTs/States of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jammu and Kashmir - Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The North-South National Highway Corridor is part of the **Golden Quadrilateral project**, which aims to connect India's four major geographical extents.
 
• The corridor spans from **Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir (North)** to **Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu (South)**.
 
• It is one of the four primary highway networks under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) initiated by the Government of India.
 
• The North-South Corridor covers a distance of approximately **4,000 kilometers**, making it one of the longest highway stretches in India.
 
• This corridor significantly boosts connectivity, trade, and transportation between India's northernmost and southernmost regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) Project**

 
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral is a highway network connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata.
 
• It was launched in 1999 under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP).
 
• The project aims to enhance connectivity between India's major cities and industrial hubs.
 
 
 
• **National Highways Development Project (NHDP)**
 
 
• NHDP is a flagship program by the Government of India for upgrading, rehabilitating, and expanding the country's highway network.
 
• It includes the Golden Quadrilateral, North-South and East-West Corridors, Port Connectivity, and other projects.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the North-South Corridor**
 
 
• It reduces travel time and transportation costs for goods and passengers.
 
• Facilitates economic integration by connecting agricultural, industrial, and urban centers across India.
 
• Boosts tourism by providing improved road access to key destinations.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Indian National Highways**
 
 
• National Highways constitute about 2% of India's road network but carry around 40% of total road traffic.
 
• They are managed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
 
• India's highways include expressways, toll roads, and standard highways to ensure efficient connectivity.
